entries.rule: Category 1: Language Keywords - Replace aerospace component-part terminology with programming language reserved words and built-in constructs. Keywords are technical nouns in code and must match the language specification exactly.
entries.ste_example: Use the `return` statement to send a value from the function.
entries.non_ste_example: The function will give back a value via the return keyword statement thing.

entries.rule: Category 2: Frameworks & Runtimes - Replace aerospace system/module names with framework and runtime identifiers. Framework names are proper nouns and must use the official capitalization.
entries.ste_example: React renders the component tree when the state changes.
entries.non_ste_example: The react framework re-renders your component tree upon state mutations occurring.

entries.rule: Category 3: Dev Tools & Build Systems - Replace aerospace tooling references with build, lint, and version control tool names. Tool names are technical nouns that refer to specific executables.
entries.ste_example: Run `eslint` to check the code for errors before you commit.
entries.non_ste_example: Make sure to run the eslint linter tool to catch any issues in your code prior to doing a commit.

entries.rule: Category 4: Dependencies & Packages - Replace aerospace part/assembly references with package and library names. Package names match the registry identifier exactly.
entries.ste_example: Install `zod` to validate the request body schema.
entries.non_ste_example: You'll want to go ahead and install the zod validation library for schema verification of request bodies.

entries.rule: Category 5: Deployment Targets - Replace aerospace vehicle/system targets with deployment platform and environment names. Each target is a proper noun identifying a specific runtime environment.
entries.ste_example: Deploy the application to the Vercel production environment.
entries.non_ste_example: The app gets shipped out to Vercel's production environment for deployment.

entries.rule: Category 6: Modules, Classes & Services - Replace aerospace subsystem names with code module, class, and service identifiers. Use PascalCase for class names as dictated by the language convention.
entries.ste_example: The `PaymentGateway` service processes transactions through the `StripeAdapter`.
entries.non_ste_example: The payment gateway service is responsible for processing of transactions utilizing the stripe adapter.

entries.rule: Category 7: Algorithmic Terms - Replace aerospace procedure/process terms with algorithm names and complexity notation. Use standard computer science terminology with exact spelling.
entries.ste_example: The binary search finds the element in O(log n) time.
entries.non_ste_example: A binary searching algorithm will locate the element with logarithmic time complexity.

entries.rule: Category 8: Routing & State - Replace aerospace navigation/routing terms with HTTP routing, middleware, and state management terms. URL paths are technical nouns and must include the leading slash.
entries.ste_example: The middleware redirects requests from `/api/v1` to `/api/v2`.
entries.non_ste_example: There is a middleware layer that will redirect incoming requests from the v1 api endpoint over to the v2 api endpoint.

entries.rule: Category 9: Data Sizes & Time - Replace aerospace measurement units with digital data sizes and time units. Use SI prefixes (kB, MB, GB) and standard time abbreviations (ms, s, min).
entries.ste_example: The query timeout is 5000 ms. The response body is 2 MB or less.
entries.non_ste_example: The query will time out after 5 seconds. Response bodies should be no larger than 2 megabytes.

entries.rule: Category 10: String Literals & Logs - Replace aerospace message/dispatch text with log messages and string literals. Quote string literals exactly as they appear in code; do not paraphrase error messages.
entries.non_ste_example: You'll see a message in the logs indicating that the connection was refused on port 5432.

entries.rule: Category 11: Roles & Teams - Replace aerospace crew/role assignments with access control roles and team identifiers. Role names are technical nouns that map to authorization policies.
entries.ste_example: Only the `admin` role can delete user accounts.
entries.non_ste_example: The administrator role is the only one that has the ability to perform deletion of user accounts.

entries.rule: Category 12: UI/UX Terms - Replace aerospace control-panel/display terms with UI component and accessibility terms. Use the standard ARIA and DOM terminology.
entries.ste_example: Set the `aria-label` attribute on the button element.
entries.non_ste_example: You should put an aria label on that button so screen readers can pick it up.

entries.rule: Category 13: Config & Preferences - Replace aerospace configuration/settings references with config file names and environment variable identifiers. Use the exact filename including extension.
entries.ste_example: Set the `DATABASE_URL` variable in the `.env` file.
entries.non_ste_example: You need to configure the database URL inside of your environment variables dot env file.

entries.rule: Category 14: Error States & Diagnostics - Replace aerospace fault/diagnostic terms with error types and failure mode names. Use the official exception class name or standard error taxonomy term exactly as it appears in the runtime.
entries.ste_example: A race condition causes the counter to show an incorrect value.
entries.non_ste_example: There's a race condition happening which results in the counter displaying wrong values.

entries.rule: Category 15: Spec Files & Manifests - Replace aerospace specification/schematic references with config file and manifest names. Use the exact filename including extension as recognized by the tool.
entries.ste_example: The `Dockerfile` copies the source code and runs the build command.
entries.non_ste_example: Your Docker file should be set up to copy over the source and then run the build step.

entries.rule: Category 16: Runtime Conditions - Replace aerospace operating condition terms with runtime state and system condition descriptors. Each condition is a discrete state, not a gradation.
entries.ste_example: The application enters read-only mode when the disk is full.
entries.non_ste_example: The application will go into a read-only type of mode if the disk becomes completely filled up.

entries.rule: Category 17: Terminal Colors - Replace aerospace color-coding terms with terminal ANSI color and style names. Use the exact ANSI attribute name or hex code as defined in the terminal emulator spec.
entries.ste_example: Set the error text color to red with ANSI code `\033[31m`.
entries.non_ste_example: Make the error messages show up in a red color using those ANSI escape code things.

entries.rule: Category 18: Bug & Defect Taxonomy - Replace aerospace defect/damage terms with vulnerability and bug class names. Use the CWE or OWASP taxonomy term exactly as published.
entries.ste_example: A SQL injection vulnerability lets an attacker run arbitrary queries.
entries.non_ste_example: There is a SQL injection type of vulnerability which allows attackers to execute any queries they want.

entries.rule: Category 19: Network & Protocol - Replace aerospace communication/signal terms with network protocol and standard names. Use the official IETF/ISO protocol designation with correct version.
entries.ste_example: The server accepts HTTP/2 connections with TLS 1.3.
entries.non_ste_example: The server is configured to accept http2 connections encrypted with tls version 1.3.
